text:
Ari: Hi team, first day laptop question. MDM shows a "FileVault required" compliance but System Settings says FileVault: Off and when I try to enable it I get an error about Secure Token. Also `fdesetup status` reports 'No user is enabled for FileVault'. Anyone seen this on macOS 14.2?

Kel (IT): Ugh, SecureToken shenanigans. Quick checks: run `sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus $(whoami)` and `fdesetup status` and paste outputs. Are you on company-created admin account or an SSO-only account?

Ari: Outputs: 
```
$ sysadminctl -secureTokenStatus ari
User ari does not have Secure Token

$ fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.
No user is enabled for FileVault.
```
I logged in with the SSO account via our Okta device-assign flow, no local admin was created.

Jo (Manager): tagging IT  Ari you're fine to wait for them to fix it, but if anyone needs a dev sandbox today we can standby on a COWorker VM.

Kel (IT): Ok this is common: MDM enrollment with SSO-only users doesn't always create a local admin with a Secure Token. Two supported paths: 1) We grant temporary local admin (preferred, quick) and use `sysadminctl -adminUser <admin> -adminPassword <pw> -secureTokenOn <user> -password <userPW>` to give your account a secure token, then MDM can enable FV. 2) IT can push an MDM command to enable FileVault via escrowed institutional recovery key (fdesetup enabling without secure token) if the device is supervised and MDM supports it. Which do you prefer?

Ari: I'd rather not get handed creds if possible. Can we do the recovery key route?

Kel (IT): Sure. I'm going to check if this device is supervised and if the MDM has FV enable with escrow path. Running inventory...

Device Bot: Device ID d7a9c2: enrolled, supervised: yes, enrollment type: DEP, MDM profile: com.redwood.mdm.enroll, FV policy: required, recovery-escrow: available.

Kel (IT): Cool, MDM supports institutional escrow. I'll push the 'Enable FileVault (escrow key)' command now. You may see a prompt asking to allow the MDM to enable FV; follow prompts and reboot when asked.

Ari: I got the prompt: "Redwood Device Management requests to enable FileVault using the organization's recovery key" with Accept / Decline. Pressed Accept. It asked for my password once, I entered it, and the UI said "FileVault enabling..."

Kel (IT): After enablement completes, run `fdesetup status` and `profiles status -type enrollment` and paste results so we can close the ticket.

Ari: After a reboot: 
```
$ fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users enabled for FileVault:
 - ari

$ profiles status -type enrollment
Enrolled: Yes
Device compliance: compliant
```
Looks good, no more prompts. Thanks!

Jo (Manager): Awesome, welcome Ari :tada: If you need short-term admin for any installs, Kel can grant a sudo window.

Kel (IT): Closing note: for others hitting this, if your account is SSO-only ask IT to either grant a temporary local admin and provision Secure Token, or push the MDM escrowed FV enable if the device is supervised. Both are acceptable; escrow route avoids sharing creds. Filing internal KB entry now.

Device Bot: Ticket #IT-1229 updated: FileVault enabled via escrow for device d7a9c2.
